newsitem.title: USA: IBM Q4 revenue gain held back by currency effect.
newsitem.headline: IBM Q4 revenue gain held back by currency effect.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp on Tuesday said its fourth-quarter revenues grew six percent year-to-year to $23.1 billion despite weakness in Europe and the negative effect of currency translation.
The company said the impact of converting revenues received in overseas currencies into U.S. dollars erased three percentage points from its fourth-quarter revenue gain.
Louis Gerstner, IBM chairman and chief executive, said: "For the full year, we grew at 9 percent in constant currency -- our highest rate of constant currency growth since 1985."

The computer maker said its gross profit margins fell to 40.3 percent from 41.7 percent in the year-ago quarter. Net earnings were $2.0 billion, or $3.93 per share. The First Call analsyts' consensus called for earnings of $3.88 per share.
It said hardware revenues rose two percent to $11.7 billion. PC and AS/400 workstation lines grew year-to-year, but mainframes declined and RS/6000 minicomputers were flat.
The company said its microelectronics, or semiconductor division, also declined. The services business grew 22 percent to $5.0 billion in the fourth quarter compared with the year-ago period.
Software revenues were $3.7 billion for the fourth quarter, up 4.0 percent from the final period of 1995.
Fourth-quarter revenues rose in North and South America, and in the Asia-Pacific region. European results were flat.
Revenues in North America increased 11 percent year over year to $9.6 billion. Asia-Pacific rose 6.0 percent to $4.3 billion, and Latin America gained 4.0 percent to $1.1 billion.
The company's revenues from Europe, Middle East and Africa were $8.1 billion, little changed year over year.
The company sold a record 1.5 million Lotus Notes seats, or licensed users, during the fourth quarter, bringing the total installed base of Notes users to nine million.
IBM said its tax rate in the fourth quarter was 29.9 percent versus 33.4 percent in the same quarter of 1995.
It said expenses declined 2.0 percent year over year.

The company said it completed the year with more than $8.0 billion in cash, after about $6.0 billion in capital expenditures, $1.0 billion in acquisitions and nearly $6.0 billion in repurchases of its common stock.
"We showed good growth in the fourth quarter despite a difficult year-over-year comparison, continued weakness in Europe and a greater-than-expected currency impact," Gerstner said in a statement.
He said IBM's storage business was "outstanding" and demand for its System/390 mainframe servers remained strong.

"Although we still face many challenges, IBM is a much different company than it was only a few years ago," he said, noting that IBM services business made up 21 percent of revenues at the end of 1996 compared with 13 percent in 1993.
IBM said "core" debt -- debt in support of operations, excluding financing -- increased $295 million from December 31, 1995, to December 31, 1996, to a total of $2.2 billion.
In the same period, debt supporting the company's worldwide credit operations grew $905 million to $20.6 billion, it said.
-- E. Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736
